newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares weather U.S. rate rise, spike up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares weather U.S. rate rise, spike up.

text.p: European stock markets speeded ahead on Wednesday after shrugging off a quarter point rise in U.S. interest rates and hints of further U.S. monetary tightening.

The dollar slipped slightly in European business but traded not far from overnight highs hit following the decision of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making open market committee to hike rates by a quarter percentage point.
Although the decision was widely expected by the markets, U.S. Treasuries were hit overnight by fears of a further Fed tightening, which dragged down European bond markets.

British government gilts opened 14/32 lower, but they inched back up after the Bank of England said its auction of 2.5 billion pounds ($4 billion) worth of 10-year bonds was covered more than three times.
Traders said the market had been hurt by Fed comments accompanying the rate rise that hinted at more action to come.
"It has made the market reassess the future of monetary policy. I think another rate rise pretty soon is now being contemplated," said one trader in London.
Despite that, European equity markets appeared to react with relief that the pre-emptive U.S. strike against inflationary pressures was out of the way.
The region's biggest bourses in London, Paris and Frankfurt led the way up in a move that was reflected in many smaller markets.
German shares made the most progress in early trade, the 30-share DAX index wiping out pre-bourse weakness to jump more than two percent during the morning.
Deutsche gained 2.42 marks to 93.67 after reporting its 1996 results and releasing an optimistic outlook for 1997.
Thyssen and Krupp were both again under the spotlight in reaction to Krupp's cancelled takeover bid, which is due to make way for a steel joint venture between the two.
Thyssen shares were quoted 0.5 marks lower at 375, while Krupp lost five marks to stand at 326.
In London, the blue chip FTSE 100 index rose more than one percent, regaining the 4,300 point level and building on Tuesday's rise that broke a six-day losing run.

"People had been reluctant to commit themselves ahead of the U.S. rate decision," said one trader. "Attention is now back on our own situation." Shares in leading retailers helped to fuel the rise after Next Plc posted strong gains following annual results at the top end of expectations, coupled with a positive trading statement. Next shares rose 27-1/2p to 623-1/2p.
Investors were likely to continue exercising caution though, traders said, with domestic interest rate and political concerns still weighing on the market and with the Easter holiday approaching.
French stocks extended their gains through the morning, boosted by shares expected to benefit from a rise in the dollar and strong corporate results.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up nearly one percent by mid-session.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar traded a little below its overnight peaks against the yen and mark.

"The tone for the dollar after the rate rise is pretty positive, though the quarter point hike was already priced in," said Jeremy Hawkins at Bank of America. "The fact we've had higher rates cemented now helps underline the divergence between the U.S. economic cycle and continental Europe."

However, analysts said the dollar was vulnerable to asset market sell-offs because of the amount of foreign investment in dollar securities, which is needed to fund the large U.S. current account deficit.
Many in the market are now looking to the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for another quarter point rise in rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1245 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6927 marks and 124.16 yen compared with 1.6919 marks and 123.92 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1245 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 44.8, or 1.05 percent, at 4,315.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was up 24.36 points, or 0.93 percent, at 2,648.61.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 68.98 points, or 2.06 percent, at 3,418.12.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed sharply lower at $346.80 versus $349.60 on Tuesday afternoon and a London close of $349.15. Silver was three cents lower at $5.10. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
